textbookText: Most of the metallic sulphides are decomposed by dilute mineral acids and produce H2S gas. In laboratory, it is prepared by the action dilute HCl or dilute H2S04 on iron sulphide. The gas is collected by upward displacement of air since it's water soluble and slightly heavier than air.

Practical Chemistry
RESULT
Hydrogen sulphide gas is prepared in laboratory by the action dilute or dilute H2S04 on iron sulphide and its properties are studied.
PRECAUTIONS
All the glasswares should be handled with care.
The lower end of the thistle funnel should dip into the acid.
The apparatus should be airtight. The gas should not be inhaled directly.
Note: Dilute HN03 cannot be used in the preparation of H2S because HN03 oxidises H2S to sulphur and it itself gets reduced to nitric oxide gas.

H2S is a weak acid. In presence of a strong acid, HCl, its ionization is decreased due to common ion effect. Hence in the acidic medium, the concentration of s Ä ions is sufficient to precipitate the sulphides of only some metal ions like Cu++, Pb++, Hg++ etc. But this concentration of - ions is not sufficient to precipitate the sulphides of other metal ions like Ni , Zn , Mn++, Co++. In case of such sulphides, the ionic product becomes less than the solubility product.
For continuous (intermittent) supply ofH2S gas in the laboratory for salt analysis and other tests, Kipp's apparatus is used to prepare this gas.
